paragraphs: His father’s name appears in Beitzah 1:9: R’ Yitzchak, R’ Lazar, in the name of R’ Immi, father of R’ Avduma of Tzippori. The supplied text calls him R’ Chani’s student, followed by the marker ב). Hyman cites Berakhot 4:3, Taanit 2:2 and Niddah 2:7 as examples of questions he put to R’ Mani. He also reports R’ Chuna in Ketubot, chapter 2, at the supplied בה״ב [contextually 2:2].

notes.text: The source calls the teacher Chani but cites questions before Mani. Its opening father-attribution list is also compressed. Neither name nor reporting link is silently repaired.

The saved whole Venice Berakhot 4:3 scalar has Rabbi Avdima of Tzippori asking Rabbi Mana. It supports the Mani question context, not the supplied teacher-name Chani or a proof of textual corruption. Avdumi/Avduma/Avdima and Mani/Mana are preserved as distinct source/named forms. No full Taanit or Niddah paragraph was returned; finite unsuccessful searches do not prove absence. The opening Yitzchak/Lazar/Immi list has no intermediate connectors, so its links are not reconstructed. The supplied ב) marker and malformed Ketubot בה״ב are retained explicitly; titles in the uninspected chain remain R'.

Hyman’s printed page has Mani both times, where the supplied text first has Chani. In Beitzah 1:9 the consulted text has Yitzchak beRabbi Lazar in the name of Immi, father of Avdoma of Tzippori. In Berakhot 4:3 and Taanit 2:2 Avduma asks Mana, while in Niddah 2:7 he speaks before Mana about the appearance of mixed wine. The same chapter separately names an Avduma of Haifa. The Chuna citation retains Hyman’s locator and attribution. The consulted Ketubot passage did not yield this attribution.
